exercise.name: Dumbbell Gorilla Row

reference.title: Dumbbell Gorilla Row (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Exhale on each row, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 0.8 s up, 0.3 s squeeze, 1 s down per side

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; stop about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2)
prescription.progression: Add load or a pause at the top

cues.text: Feet wide, toes out, hips back and low, back flat and nearly level, a dumbbell under each shoulder between the feet.
Breathe out and row one dumbbell up inside the knee to the side of the lower ribs; the other hand presses its dumbbell into the floor.
Squeeze the shoulder blade back; shoulders and hips stay square.
Lower under control until the dumbbell rests on the floor again.
Both dumbbells down, keep the hinge, then row the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk to heave the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders level; use lighter dumbbells.
Hold the hips back and the back flat for the whole set.
Bend the knees more and keep the chest proud.

kinematics.norm: Deep hinge, back flat and close to level (clinical opinion)
Knees bent and pushed out over the toes in the wide stance (clinical opinion)
From nearly straight to well bent at the top, the elbow driving up past the back (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 1 s down per side (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1124112, Dumbbell Gorilla Row (male), video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain: a bench-supported row loads the back less (Fenwick 2009).
modify: Tight hamstrings: bend the knees more.
Shoulder pain: shorten the top of the row.
regressions: One-arm dumbbell row on a bench.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Main shoulder extensor: pulls the elbow from below the shoulder back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Main shoulder extensor: pulls the elbow from below the shoulder back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top; rows gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of the pulls tested by Lehman 2004.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top; rows gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of the pulls tested by Lehman 2004.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps extend the shoulder as the elbow passes the trunk.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps extend the shoulder as the elbow passes the trunk.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Flexes the elbow; the neutral grip shares the work with brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Flexes the elbow; the neutral grip shares the work with brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the deep hinge with a flat back; the standing bent-over row had the highest lumbar load of the rows compared by Fenwick 2009.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the deep hinge with a flat back; the standing bent-over row had the highest lumbar load of the rows compared by Fenwick 2009.
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the trunk stays square while one side lifts.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist trunk rotation from the one-sided row (Fenwick 2009, one-armed row).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist trunk rotation from the one-sided row (Fenwick 2009, one-armed row).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hold the hips back in the wide stance.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hold the hips back in the wide stance.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: The support arm stays long and presses its dumbbell into the floor.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: The support arm stays long and presses its dumbbell into the floor.

guides.label: Elbow bent, high and back at the top
